description: The meter's first night on the rig, 15 h 39 m: 277 raw edges from gpiomon v2.2.1 (both edges, bias pull-up, NO debounce, realtime clock) on GPIO 27, with the Pi's internal pull-up only. 15 edges, in 8 clusters, are microsecond spikes that report the level the line already had, most within a second of the boiler programmer switching CH or HW. Draws: a bath (35 L) and its top-up (23 L), a slow tap (9 L), three sinks (2 L each), a shower (56 L), and two lone pulses (at +0:33:41 and +15:38:55). Counting every falling edge gives 140. Times are shifted to start at 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z (a whole number of seconds, so every interval is as recorded).
source: real capture: gpiomon -c gpiochip0 -b pull-up -E realtime -F '%S %e' 27; lines are epoch_seconds.ns and the edge (1 rising = opens, 2 falling = closes)
anchors_why: 452 ms: the first bath litre. 26.989 s: the slow tap's wheel paused mid-turn. 4 h 26 m 26.631 s: the pointer resting on the magnet from +0:33:41 (counted) to +5:00:08, through two spikes. 32 m 20.211 s: the sink's last litre, resting until +5:32:56. 1.832 s: the first bath interval.
